title: Real conversation
goal: Tell a friend what happened, react while they tell you their news, pass on what people said and keep a chat going.
intro:
This is the last unit of Part 1, and it's about the thing you've been working towards: **real conversation**. You'll learn how Tamil speakers tell a friend what happened (**தெரியுமா, நேத்து என்ன நடந்துச்சுன்னு?** 'you know what happened yesterday?'), how listeners react (**நிஜமாவா?**, **அச்சச்சோ!**, **செம!**), and the little words that keep a chat moving (**அப்புறம்**, **அதாவது**, **சும்மா**, **சரி விடு**).

Two structures let you build longer sentences: **relative clauses**, where the verb comes before the noun (**நான் பாத்த படம்** 'the film I saw'), and **reported speech** with **-ன்னு** (**வர்றேன்னு சொன்னான்** 'he said he'd come'). You'll also meet the way friends talk to each other: **மச்சான்**, **டா** and **டி**.

vocab.note: a storytelling opener: தெரியுமா, அப்புறம்…
spoken: கடைசில kaḍaisila

vocab.en: that is to say, I mean

vocab.note: written நிஜமாக nijamāga; as a question நிஜமாவா? "really?"
softer than ஐயோ; for a spilt coffee or a missed bus

vocab.en: oh wow! oh dear! (surprise or sympathy)

vocab.note: அவன் பாவம் "poor guy"
நம்பவே முடியல "I just can't believe it"
young people's favourite intensifier: செம படம் "a great film", செம பசி "starving"; also spelt செம்ம
யாராவது yārāvadu "anyone"; யாரும் + negative "no one"
ஏதாவது ēdāvadu "anything"; ஏதோ சோகமா இருக்க "you seem kind of down"
அவன் மாதிரி "like him"; நான் சொன்ன மாதிரி "the way I said"

phrases.en: I mean, what I'm trying to say is…
The film I saw yesterday was great.
He said he'd come tomorrow. (lit. "I'm coming," he said)
I was only joking, don't be offended. (polite)
OK, where was I? (lit. where did I leave off?)

grammar.title: Relative clauses: the verb goes before the noun
grammar.body:
Tamil has **no relative pronouns** ('who', 'which', 'that'). Instead the verb of the clause takes an adjective ending, **-அ**, and goes **before** the noun it describes: நான் **பாத்த** படம் 'the film I saw' (lit. 'I saw-which film').

**Past**: past stem + -அ — வந்த *vanda* 'that came', பாத்த *pātta* 'that (someone) saw', சொன்ன *sonna* 'that (someone) said', வாங்கின *vāngina* 'that (someone) bought'
**Present**: present stem + -அ — வர்ற *varra* 'that comes / is coming', இருக்கிற *irukkira* 'that is', படிக்கிற *paḍikkira* 'that studies'
**Future / general**: -உம் — வரும் *varum* 'that will come', பிடிக்கும் 'that (someone) likes'
**Negative**: -ஆத — வராத *varāda* 'that doesn't / didn't come', தெரியாத *teriyāda* 'unknown'

The form never changes for person or number, and the clause can be as long as you like: **நேத்து நீ ஃபோன்ல சொன்ன** கடை 'the shop you mentioned on the phone yesterday'.

Add **-து** to the past or present form to make a noun, 'what / the one that / the fact that': நீ சொன்ன**து** 'what you said', நடந்த**து** 'what happened', அவன் வந்த**து** எனக்குத் தெரியாது 'I didn't know he'd come'.

The trap: don't look for a word for 'who'. யாரு is only a question word; 'the man who came' is simply **வந்த ஆளு**.

examples.en: my elder sister who lives in Chennai
The guy who phoned yesterday is here.
There's no food I don't like.

grammar.title: Reported speech with -ன்னு
grammar.body:
Tamil prefers **direct** quotation. You repeat what someone said in their own words, close it with **-ன்னு** *-nnu* (written என்று *endru*), then add the speech verb: அவன் 'வர்றேன்' **-ன்னு** சொன்னான் → அவன் **வர்றேன்னு** சொன்னான் 'He said he'd come' (lit. 'I'm coming, he said').

The quoted verb keeps the **original speaker's person**: அவரு **வர்றேன்னு** சொன்னாரு, with the *I*-ending, means 'he said that he would come'. If you say அவரு **வருவாருன்னு** சொன்னாரு, it normally means he said some *other* man would come.

**Commands** are reported with the infinitive + **சொல்லு**: என்னை **வர** சொன்னாங்க 'they told me to come', அம்மா **சாப்பிட** சொன்னாங்க 'Mum told (me) to eat'.
**Questions** keep their -ஆ or question word: **வர்றீங்களான்னு** கேட்டாங்க 'they asked if you're coming', **எப்போ வருவீங்கன்னு** கேட்டாரு 'he asked when you'd come'.
**Hearsay** works the same way: லீவு**ன்னு** கேள்விப்பட்டேன் 'I heard it's a holiday'.

In chats and subtitles you'll often see it written with a single ன: **-னு** (வர்றேனு, சரினு). The trap: don't translate English 'that' with anything else; -ன்னு is the only 'that' you need.

examples.en: What do you call this in Tamil?
I heard that tomorrow is a holiday.

grammar.title: Telling it and keeping it going: connectors, reactions and -தான் / -உம் / -ஏ
grammar.body:
A story told to a friend hangs on a few small words:

**Opening**: **தெரியுமா?** 'you know what?', **ஒரு விஷயம்…** 'listen to this…'
**Moving on**: **அப்புறம்** 'then, and so', **திடீர்னு** 'suddenly', **அதனால** 'so', **ஆனா** 'but', **இருந்தாலும்** 'even so', **கடைசில** 'in the end'
**Explaining**: **அதாவது** 'I mean', **சொல்லப்போனா** 'actually', **சும்மா** 'just, for no reason'
**Losing the thread**: **நான் எங்க விட்டேன்?** 'where was I?'

The listener works just as hard: **ம்ம்**, **ஆமா**, **அப்புறம்?** 'and then?', **நிஜமாவா?** 'really?', **அப்படியா?** 'is that so?', **அச்சச்சோ!** / **ஐயோ!** for bad news, **பாவம்!** 'poor thing!', **அடடா!** / **செம!** for good news.

Three particles add nuance to any word: **-தான்** *-dān* 'exactly, it's… that' (**நான்தான்** சொன்னேன் 'it was me who said it', அப்படி**த்தான்** 'that's just how it is'); **-உம்** *-um* 'also, too; and; even' (**நானும்** வர்றேன் 'I'm coming too'); **-ஏ** *-ē* 'the very; at all' (**இப்போவே** 'right now', நம்ப**வே** முடியல 'I just can't believe it').

examples.en: It was me who said it.
It's hard, sure, but we'll give it a go anyway.

dialogue.title: You won't believe who pushed my car
dialogue.setting: Karthik meets his friend Priya at a tea stall in Besant Nagar, Chennai, the evening after a big downpour.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.native: என்னடா, என்ன விஷயம்? ஏதோ சோகமா இருக்க.
lines.roman: ennaḍā, enna vishayam? ēdō sōgamā irukka.
lines.en: Hey, what's up? You look kind of down.

lines.speaker: Karthik
lines.native: அதை ஏன் கேக்குற! நேத்து என்ன ஆச்சு தெரியுமா?
lines.roman: adai ēn kēkkura! nēttu enna ācchu teriyumā?
lines.en: Don't even ask! You know what happened yesterday?

lines.speaker: Karthik
lines.native: அப்பாவோட காரை எடுத்துட்டு வேளச்சேரிக்குப் போனேன். திடீர்னு செம மழை.
lines.roman: appāvōḍa kārai eḍuttuṭṭu Vēḷacchērikkup pōnēn. tiḍīrnu sema maḻai.
lines.en: I took Dad's car to Velachery. Suddenly it absolutely poured.

lines.speaker: Karthik
lines.native: கார் நடு ரோட்டுல நின்னுடுச்சு. ஒருத்தர் வந்து தள்ளி விட்டாரு.
lines.roman: kār naḍu rōṭṭula ninnuḍucchu. oruttar vandu taḷḷi viṭṭāru.
lines.en: The car died in the middle of the road. Someone came and gave it a push.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.en: You poor thing! Who was he?

lines.speaker: Karthik
lines.native: அதான் விஷயம்! நம்ம ஸ்கூல்ல கணக்கு சொல்லிக்குடுத்த ராஜா சார்!
lines.roman: adān vishayam! namma skūlla kaṇakku sollikkuḍutta Rājā sār!
lines.en: That's the thing! Raja sir, who taught us maths at school!

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.native: நிஜமாவா? நம்பவே முடியல! அவருக்கு உன்னை ஞாபகம் இருந்துச்சா?
lines.roman: nijamāvā? nambavē muḍiyala! avarukku unnai ñābagam irunducchā?
lines.en: Seriously? No way! Did he remember you?

lines.speaker: Karthik
lines.en: He did! He asked, "Are you still always late?"

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.native: ஹா ஹா! செம கிண்டல்! கடைசில கார் ஸ்டார்ட் ஆச்சா?
lines.roman: hā hā! sema kiṇḍal! kaḍaisila kār sṭārṭ ācchā?
lines.en: Ha ha! Brilliant! Did the car start in the end?

lines.speaker: Karthik
lines.en: It did. But don't tell Dad, OK?

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.native: சரி விடு, நான் ஒண்ணும் சொல்ல மாட்டேன். ஆனா டீ நீதான் வாங்கணும்!
lines.roman: sari viḍu, nān oṇṇum solla māṭṭēn. ānā ṭī nīdān vāngaṇum!
lines.en: Fine, I won't say a word. But you're buying the tea!

culture: In a Tamil conversation the listener is never silent. People keep up a stream of **ம்ம்**, **ஆமா**, **அப்புறம்?** and **அச்சச்சோ!**, and finish each other's sentences; listening quietly can come across as bored or cold. Among friends of the same age the talk gets very informal: **நீ**, bare commands (சொல்லு, வா), **டா** to a guy and **டி** to a girl (என்னடா?, வாடி!), and **மச்சான்** or **மச்சி** between mates. These are warm, not rude, between friends, but use them with an elder, a shopkeeper or your friend's parents and it sounds shocking: there it's **நீங்க**, **-ங்க** and **அண்ணா / அக்கா**. Young people in Chennai mix English freely (*செம டென்ஷன்*, *ஃபுல் ஜாலி*), quote film dialogue and tease each other constantly (**கலாய்**), so if your sentences come out half English, you're sounding like everyone else. When a friend shares news, ask **வேற என்ன விசேஷம்?** 'what else is new?' and the chat keeps going. From here, Part 2 takes you into real life: making plans, calls, getting around town, eating out and much more.

tip.title: Telling it: அப்புறம் → திடீர்னு → கடைசில
tip.body:
- Open with **தெரியுமா?** 'you know what?' to grab attention.
- Move the story on with **அப்புறம்** 'then', **திடீர்னு** 'suddenly', and close with **கடைசில** 'in the end'.
- **இருந்தாலும்** 'even so' adds a twist; **அதாவது** 'I mean' corrects yourself.
- Tell it in the simple past: போனேன், பாத்தேன், ஆச்சு.

sentences.native: நேத்து ஆஃபீஸ்ல ஒரு விஷயம் நடந்துச்சு, தெரியுமா?
sentences.roman: nēttu āfīsla oru vishayam naḍanducchu, teriyumā?
sentences.en: Something happened at the office yesterday, you know?
Akka, you know what happened yesterday?

sentences.native: நான் பஸ்ல ஏறினேன், அப்புறம்தான் காசு இல்லன்னு தெரிஞ்சுது.
sentences.roman: nān basla ērinēn, appuramdān kāsu illannu terinjudu.
sentences.en: I got on the bus, and only then did I realise I had no money.
Suddenly the power went off.
In the end we went home by auto.

sentences.native: ரொம்ப லேட் ஆயிடுச்சு, இருந்தாலும் படம் பாத்தோம்.
sentences.roman: romba lēṭ āyiḍucchu, irundālum paḍam pāttōm.
sentences.en: It got really late, but we watched the film anyway.

sentences.native: அவ என் ஃப்ரெண்ட், அதாவது என் ஃப்ரெண்டோட தங்கச்சி.
sentences.roman: ava en freṇḍ, adāvadu en freṇḍōḍa tangacchi.
sentences.en: She's my friend, I mean my friend's younger sister.
And then? What did he say?
Then what happened? Did he come in the end?

sentences.native: அதாவது, நான் என்ன சொல்ல வர்றேன்னா, அவன் மேல தப்பு இல்ல.
sentences.roman: adāvadu, nān enna solla varrēnnā, avan mēla tappu illa.
sentences.en: I mean, what I'm trying to say is, it's not his fault.

tip.title: React, react, react
tip.body:
- A Tamil listener is never silent: **ம்ம்**, **ஆமா**, **அப்புறம்?** keep the speaker going.
- Surprise: **நிஜமாவா?**, **அப்படியா?** · Bad news: **அச்சச்சோ!**, **ஐயோ!**, **பாவம்!** · Good news: **அடடா!**, **செம!**
- **நம்பவே முடியல** 'I just can't believe it': the **-ஏ** on நம்ப adds 'at all'.

sentences.en: Oh no, did your phone break?
Are you serious? (lit. are you saying it truly?)
He got the job? Awesome!
Oh wow, that's great news!
Poor thing, it must have been really hard for her.
Believe me, I'm not lying! (informal)
I didn't believe him.

sentences.native: நிஜமாவா? நம்பவே முடியல! அவரு உன்கிட்ட பேசினாரா?
sentences.roman: nijamāvā? nambavē muḍiyala! avaru unkiṭṭa pēsinārā?
sentences.en: Really? I can't believe it! He actually talked to you?
Oh no, and then? How did you get home?
Great film, you have to watch it!

tip.title: The one who…: verb before the noun
tip.body:
- Tamil has no 'who / which'. Put the verb, with **-அ**, **before** the noun: நான் **பாத்த** படம் 'the film I saw'.
- Past: வந்த, சொன்ன, பாத்த · Now: வர்ற, நிக்கிற · Not: வராத, தெரியாத.
- Add **-து** for 'what / the one that': நீ சொன்ன**து** 'what you said'.

sentences.native: நேத்து நான் பாத்த பொண்ணு உன் ஃப்ரெண்டா?
sentences.roman: nēttu nān pātta poṇṇu un freṇḍā?
sentences.en: Is the girl I saw yesterday your friend?
Where's the shop you mentioned?
Who's that guy who's always laughing?
I remember what you said.
Do it the way I told you.

sentences.native: நேத்து உங்க வீட்டுக்கு வந்த பையன் பேரு என்ன?
sentences.roman: nēttu unga vīṭṭukku vanda paiyan pēru enna?
sentences.en: What's the name of the guy who came to your place yesterday?

sentences.native: தமிழ் தெரியாத என் ஃப்ரெண்டுக்கும் அந்தப் படம் பிடிச்சுது.
sentences.roman: tamiḻ teriyāda en freṇḍukkum andap paḍam piḍicchudu.
sentences.en: Even my friend who doesn't know Tamil liked that film.

sentences.native: நான் நேத்து பாத்த படம் சூப்பர், நீயும் பாரு.
sentences.roman: nān nēttu pātta paḍam sūppar, nīyum pāru.
sentences.en: The film I saw yesterday was great, you should see it too.
Do you know who that guy standing over there is?
Someone called you.
He said something, I didn't get it.

sentences.native: எனக்கு ஞாபகம் இல்ல, ஏதோ ஒரு கடை.
sentences.roman: enakku ñābagam illa, ēdō oru kaḍai.
sentences.en: I don't remember, some shop or other.

tip.title: Quote it, then -ன்னு + சொன்னான்
tip.body:
- Repeat the words as they were said, add **-ன்னு**, then the verb: அவன் 'வர்றேன்'**னு** சொன்னான் 'he said he'd come'.
- The quoted verb keeps the speaker's 'I': **வர்றேன்னு**, not வருவான்னு.
- Commands: infinitive + **சொல்லு**: என்னை **வர** சொன்னாங்க 'they told me to come'.
- **கேள்விப்பட்டேன்** 'I heard (that)…' works the same way.

sentences.en: She said she'd be late.
He said he was hungry.

sentences.native: அம்மா உன்னை சீக்கிரம் வீட்டுக்கு வர சொன்னாங்க.
sentences.roman: ammā unnai sīkkiram vīṭṭukku vara sonnānga.
sentences.en: Mum told you to come home early.
I heard the two of them had a fight.
I don't remember what he said.
He said he couldn't get tickets.
They asked if you're coming.
Who told you to do it like this?

sentences.native: அவரு நாளைக்கு வர்றேன்னு சொன்னாரு, ஆனா எனக்கு நம்பிக்கை இல்ல.
sentences.roman: avaru nāḷaikku varrēnnu sonnāru, ānā enakku nambikkai illa.
sentences.en: He said he'd come tomorrow, but I'm not convinced.

sentences.native: சார், மேடம் உங்களை உள்ள வர சொன்னாங்க.
sentences.roman: sār, mēḍam ungaḷai uḷḷa vara sonnānga.
sentences.en: Sir, madam asked you to come in.
He never said that!

tip.title: மச்சான், டா, டி: only with friends
tip.body:
- With close friends your own age Tamil gets very informal: **நீ**, bare commands (சொல்லு, வா), and **டா** to a guy / **டி** to a girl, glued on: என்ன**டா**? 'what, man?'
- Guys call each other **மச்சான்** 'bro'.
- Slang everyone uses: **செம** 'awesome', **மொக்கை** 'lame', **ஜாலி** 'fun'.
- With elders and strangers it's back to **நீங்க** and **-ங்க**.

sentences.en: Hey man, how are you?
Bro, how was the film yesterday?
The film was so lame, man!
Hey, why are you late? (to a female friend)
Stop teasing, man, I mean it.
They always make fun of me.
It was so much fun at the beach yesterday!
This is my school friend.
Chill, don't worry!
OK bro, see you later.

tip.title: Small words that keep it moving
tip.body:
- **என்ன விஷயம்?** 'what's up?' · **வேற என்ன விசேஷம்?** 'what else is new?'
- Lost the thread? **நான் எங்க விட்டேன்?** 'where was I?'
- Dropping a topic: **சரி விடு** 'forget it' (polite: விடுங்க).
- **சும்மா** 'just, for no reason' takes the edge off: சும்மா கேட்டேன் 'just asking'.

sentences.en: What's up? Why did you call? (informal)
What else is new at home?
Just asking, nothing else.
Stop it, man! / Keep quiet!

sentences.native: சரி விடு, அது பெரிய விஷயம் இல்ல.
sentences.roman: sari viḍu, adu periya vishayam illa.
sentences.en: Forget it, it's no big deal.
Leave him, he's just like that.
Actually, I didn't like that film.

sentences.native: ஓகே, நான் எங்க விட்டேன்? ஆ, அப்புறம் அவன் வந்தான்…
sentences.roman: ōkē, nān enga viṭṭēn? ā, appuram avan vandān…
sentences.en: OK, where was I? Ah, then he turned up…

sentences.native: சொல்லு, சொல்லு! அப்புறம் அவ என்ன சொன்னா?
sentences.roman: sollu, sollu! appuram ava enna sonnā?
sentences.en: Go on, go on! Then what did she say?
I was only joking, don't be upset, akka.
